questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to go to the US, and I heard that Boston was great place to study abroad. Boston is a city with many different and well renowned universities which motivated me to choose Boston University as my first priority. Moreover, the city is very European in some aspects which also was one of the main reasons why I chose this university compared to others in the US. Furthermore, there is many people in Boston who come from different cultures all over the world which further enhanced my dedication in choosing this university among others.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you have the time and the money, I would highly recommend to study abroad. I have developed a lot as a person and met many interesting people from all over the world (eg. US, India, Colombia ect.). The professors are also enthusiastic and are alway there to help if you are having difficulty with something. I stayed in a hotel for the entire exchange, which meant that our room was nicely decorated and always clean (I didn't pay more for this, as the university provided this).

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to some point. We had some meetings with exchange manager at Boston University, and they also had a website that listed everything we needed to do and know before arrival. You will get an email where you will receive all important information regarding the exchange. Note, that they are a bit slow to respond to emails which was quite annoying.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We got an introduction to the university the first three days of the exchange. Here we met with others who were on exchange and learned a little about the university and their inclusion.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of different options regarding housing. You can choose to live alone or with someone and if you want the meal plan or make your own food. The cheapest option is to live with someone and I don't know if you can live alone in upcoming semesters, as they are renovating many dorms [Warren Towers] why there may be a lack of housing supply.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You can choose a meal plan where you get access to a buffet like dining hall. There are 5 different ones [Fenway was the best!]. If you would rather cook yourself, you can choose an apartment style housing where there is a small kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Because of low housing supply I and most exchange and transfer students stayed at a hotel [Hyatt Regency Cambridge]. This was very nice. I also opted for the meal plan and I would also recommend you doing that, as groceries in the US are quite expensive. Moreover, you will get some dining points with the dining plan where you can use them for Starbucks, Panda Express, Dominos and many more.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a problem that every exchange student encountered while registering for courses. BU had just changed IT systems, why it took very long before we could even register for the courses. This meant that some of the courses that I wanted to take were filled up, meaning that I had to be on a waiting list.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: More or less the same as UCPH. You sign into your BU account and get a list of different courses you can choose from. It says if they are full or available. If they are full, you can get on the waiting list [If it is not full], and if it is available you can enroll right away. Some courses may have prerequisites, but they often don't ask if you have had these courses. However, I would not recommend you choosing something totally new.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange student manager [Sage] was helpful with the process and if you encountered any problems you were always welcome to send her an email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty successful with the process. There was only one course that I didn't get, but that was alright. I was on the waiting list for two of the courses I wanted, but I only got a place on one course [Game Theory].

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Even though you are on the waiting list at the very start of the semester, I would highly recommend not to remove yourself from the waiting list. I was number 13 or something in July for Game Theory and was quite anxious if I got that but two weeks before the semester started I eventually got enrolled in the courses. Moreover, you can always talk to the professors. They may be more susceptible to let exchange students enroll in courses that are full.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses were easier than others. Undergraduate courses (Level 400 and below) was easier than undergraduate courses at UCPH. On the other hand, graduate courses are somewhat more difficult than the undergraduate. I would say they are more like the level we have at UCHP or even harder. I had one [EC531] which was quite hard.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Undergraduate courses are easier while graduate courses are similar or even harder.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Urban & Regional Economics [CASEC 328]
Game Theory [CASEC 403]
Market Structure & Industrial Organization [CASEC 531]

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Would recommend Urban & Regional Economics if you want something with less math but that works with some exciting topics. Game Theory was also pretty good and the professor was good. I took it as a substitute to Micro III. If you like theory and math (Like Micro I), I would recommend Market Structure & Industrial Organization.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The is some vaccines you have to get, but you can get them for free though the insurance. I would highly recommend doing that and save the money [I paid around 3,000 DKK for the vaccines].

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Prices were as expected. Boston is an expensive city, so if you want to grab a drink or eat out, you can expect the same prices as Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many different kind of cultural, athletic and social activities available for the students at the university. Trivia nights, bingo and so on. You can also sign up for different sports activities such as long distance running, sailing, rugby, volleyball, football [soccer] and so on. They have a huge gym where there are plenty of opportunities to do all kinds of sports (Swimming, climbing, weightlifting).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you like to run, I would recommend joining the long distance running club. It is a great way to start your day, but it is also a great opportunity to meet new people. If you want to meet new people in general, join one of the many student activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Many people traveled to New York City for a weekend trip. If you have never seen it and it is on your bucket list, I would highly suggest going, as it is only a 3-4 hour drive from Boston. During Thanksgiving, I and 9 other exchange students and fellow friends from Denmark traveled to Maine (Further north than Boston). If you want to go out of town and see some beautiful nature, I would endorse Maine and see Acadia National Park. [Note that we rented cars through Turo with was the easiest]. While you're in Boston, you should also walk the Freedom Trail and see some of their museums, especially Isabella Stewart Gardner.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to say the least. It will take maybe two weeks or so to get used to it completely. Economics at UCPH only lectures only in courses in Danish, why it takes some time to get used to it. However, most master courses are in fact lectured in English, why study abroad ultimately helps you in your future studies.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Students are very sweet and open and in some courses there are group projects where you will get a study group. I would also recommend to share a dorm with others as this is a great opportunity to get to know others. As mentioned above, you can also join one of the many fitness clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find anything particular challenging. You just had to get used to the currency, language, and their tipping culture. The tipping was probably the hardest, as we are never used to do it in Denmark. But you will figure it out while you are there.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People's openness. They are so nice in the US and comments if they like your shoes and what not. You will never hear a Dane say this. Moreover, the professors at BU comes from all over the world and the same is true for the students. I really appreciated this as I gained insight into new cultures in relation to my own.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: If you want to try something new in relation to UCPH, where you can improve yourself as a person, meet new people and get to know new cultures, and at the same time get an experience of a lifetime, I would definitely recommend you go. It's worth it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend you at least try Fenway dining hall once for dinner. It won't disappoint you. I would also recommend buying a power outlet, as it is quite useful. If I were you I would get the dining plan

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends and the personal development. As I have already pointed out, this is an experience of a lifetime.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was probably leaving Denmark and say goodbye to friends and family. It was nerve-racking and I was afraid of being lonely and not meet anyone. But once I arrived and met my roommate, this nervousness was already gone. You have to know that everyone is in the same boat.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
